chapters.title: 一 · 一个极简的办法
二 · 芯片里的同一个问题
第 2 层 · 怎样算最强
第 3 层 · 一次更新
第 5 层 · 何时停止
第 6 层 · 同时还是轮流
第 7 层 · 分得好不好
第 8 层 · 回到芯片
第 9 层 · 它做不到的事

transcript.text: 打开通讯录，几百个名字。
要把他们分成几个圈子，你会怎么分？
你不需要知道每个人是谁，
只要看：谁和谁常联系。
好的分组：圈内联系紧，圈与圈之间联系少。
网络科学把这件事叫作“社群发现”。
2007 年，三位研究者提出一个极简的办法。
每个人看看朋友们现在属于哪个圈子，
然后加入联系最多的那一个。
一遍遍重复，圈子自己浮现。
同样的问题，藏在每一块芯片里。
几百万个单元，由导线连成一张网。
设计时，EDA 软件要先把它们分成几块。
为什么要在乎怎么分？
同一块里的单元，用短导线相连。
分在两块的单元，只能靠长导线。
导线越长，信号越慢，也越耗电。
所以目标和通讯录一样：块内紧，块间少。
看一个 24 个单元的小例子。
最直接的办法：拿尺子，按位置切成三块。
很整齐。可它切断了多少连线？
切断的权重是 88，全部 202：将近一半。
那就试遍所有分法，挑最好的？
24 个单元平分三组，约 15.8 亿种分法。
上百万个单元呢？分法的数字有 47 万位。
一个个试，永远试不完。
那就借用通讯录里的那条规则：
每个单元看看邻居们现在的标签，
加入连接最强的那一组。
这就是标签传播。
规则只有一句话，细节却很要紧：
“最强”怎么算？谁先更新？
什么时候停？它一定会停吗？
下半部分，用老师给的五节点图，一层层拆开。
停在这里想一想：如果是你，会怎么回答？
九层，从浅到深。
第一层：标签。
开始时，每个点的标签就是自己的名字。
名字是身份，永远不变；
标签是归属，会被改写。
第二层：“最强”怎么算？
A 的三个邻居里，B 和 C 带着标签 B，D 带着 D。
数人头，B 两票；加权重，B 只有 2，D 有 4。
所以规则是：把同标签邻居的边权加起来，取最大。
第三层：一次更新。看 C。
邻居 A、B 已经是 B；D 是 D，E 是 E。
同标签先相加：B 是 1 + 4 = 5，D 是 2，E 是 1。
第四层：一整轮，按 A 到 E 依次更新。
B 立刻读到 A 的新标签：这叫异步更新。
C 改为 B，就是刚才那一步。
D 改为 E，E 保持。第一轮结束。
第五层：什么时候停？再问一遍每个点。
整整一轮，没有一个点改变。
只有整轮零变化，才能确认稳定。
否则后面的点一改，前面的点可能又要改。
第六层：如果所有点同时更新呢？
两个点，各自读对方的旧标签——
A 变成 B，B 变成 A，再换回来：永远停不下来。
轮流更新时，B 读到 A 的新标签，两者一致。
第七层：分得好不好？看被切开的边。
C–D 权重 2，C–E 权重 1。
cutsize 是被切开的权重之和：2 + 1 = 3。
把 C–D 加强到 10，边界立刻移动。
第八层：回到 24 个单元，每个从自己的标签出发。
颜色沿着最强的连线扩散。
每一轮只读每条连线两次：工作量和连线数成正比。
第 5 轮零变化。只切开 2，尺子切开 88。
第九层：它做不到的事。
它不保证分成几组，也不保证每组一样大。
换个访问顺序，标签名和轮数都可能变。
它给出的是线索，不是最终答案。
在芯片设计中，聚类常用来先把紧密的单元收成团，
让电路图变小，再交给更精细的划分与布局。
通讯录里的圈子，芯片里的分块，是同一个问题。
没有人画圈。圈子，从连接里长出来。
去实验室改一条边的权重，看看边界会怎么走。

chapters.title: II · THE SAME PROBLEM IN A CHIP
III · THE RULER AND BRUTE FORCE
LAYER 6 · ALL AT ONCE, OR IN TURN

transcript.text: Open your contacts: hundreds of names.
How would you sort them into circles?
You don't need to know who anyone is.
Just look at who keeps in touch with whom.
A good grouping: tight inside, few links between.
Network science calls this community detection.
In 2007, three researchers proposed a strikingly simple method.
Each person checks which circle their friends are in now,
and joins the one they are most connected to.
Repeat, and the circles appear on their own.
The same problem hides inside every chip.
Millions of cells, wired into one network.
To design it, EDA software first splits them into blocks.
Why does the split matter?
Cells in the same block connect with short wires.
Cells in different blocks need long wires.
Longer wires mean slower signals and more power.
So the goal matches your contacts: tight inside, few between.
Take a small example: 24 cells.
The obvious approach: a ruler, three blocks by position.
Neat. But how much wiring does it cut?
It cuts weight 88 out of 202: almost half.
Then why not try every split and keep the best?
24 cells into three equal groups: about 1.58 billion ways.
A million cells? The count itself has 477,121 digits.
Trying them one by one would never finish.
So borrow the rule from your contacts:
each cell looks at its neighbours' current labels,
and joins the group it is most strongly wired to.
This is label propagation.
One sentence of rule, but the details matter:
What counts as strongest? Who updates first?
When does it stop? Does it always stop?
In part two, we take it apart layer by layer on the teacher's five-node graph.
Pause here: how would you answer them?
Nine layers, from shallow to deep.
Layer one: labels.
At the start, every node's label is its own name.
The name is its identity and never changes;
the label is where it belongs, and it can be rewritten.
Layer two: what counts as strongest?
Of A's three neighbours, B and C carry label B, D carries D.
By headcount B has two votes; by weight B has 2 and D has 4.
So the rule: add up edge weights per label, take the largest.
Layer three: one update. Watch C.
Neighbours A and B already carry B; D carries D, E carries E.
Same labels add up first: B is 1 + 4 = 5, D is 2, E is 1.
Layer four: a full round, A to E in order.
B already sees A's new label: this is asynchronous updating.
C becomes B, the step we just saw.
D becomes E, E stays. Round one ends.
Layer five: when to stop? Ask every node again.
A whole round, and no node changes.
Only a full round with zero changes confirms it is stable.
Otherwise a later change could force an earlier node to change again.
Layer six: what if every node updates at once?
Two nodes, each reading the other's old label...
A becomes B, B becomes A, and back again: it never stops.
Taking turns, B reads A's new label and they agree.
Layer seven: is the split good? Look at the cut edges.
C–D has weight 2, C–E has weight 1.
Cutsize is the sum of cut weights: 2 + 1 = 3.
Strengthen C–D to 10 and the boundary moves.
Layer eight: back to the 24 cells, each starting with its own label.
Colour spreads along the strongest wires.
Each round reads every wire twice: the work grows with the number of wires.
Round 5: no changes. It cuts 2; the ruler cut 88.
Layer nine: what it cannot do.
It promises neither the number of groups nor equal sizes.
Change the visiting order and label names and round counts can change.
It gives a clue, not a final answer.
In chip design, clustering often first gathers tightly wired cells,
shrinking the netlist before finer partitioning and placement.
Circles in your contacts and blocks in a chip are the same problem.
No one draws the circles. They grow out of the connections.
Open the lab, change one edge weight, and watch the boundary move.

transcript.text: 一张带权图：线越粗，连接越强。
目标：把连接紧密的点分到一组，而且不事先说分几组。
规则只有一句：看邻居现在的标签，
加入边权之和最大的那一组。
每次只看一个点和它的邻居。
先分清两个词：名字是身份，永远不变；
标签是归属，可以改写。
开始时，每个点的标签就是自己的名字。
轮到 C。A 已经改为标签 B。
同一标签的边权加起来。
B = 5，D = 2，E = 1：C 的标签改为 B。
比的是权重之和，不是邻居个数。
异步更新：按 A→E 依次来，改完立刻生效。
A：改为 B。
B：保持 B。
C：改为 B。
D：改为 E。
E：保持 E。
第 1 轮改了 3 个点。
第 2 轮：每个点再投一次。
一个都没变，这才确认稳定：共 2 轮，cut 3。
停止有三种：stable，完整一轮零变化；
cycle，状态重复出现；
limit，到了轮数上限。只有 stable 才叫收敛。
换成同步更新：大家读同一张旧快照。
A 读到 B，B 读到 A，同时交换，再换回来。
状态重复：这是 cycle，不是收敛。
三个旋钮会改变结果。
反过来访问：3 轮，标签名变了，分组不变。
把 C–D 加到 10：分组变成 AB | CDE，cut 5。
记住四点。
快、局部、不需要 K；
但结果依赖规则，
也不保证均衡。下面的实验里亲手试一遍。
A weighted graph: the thicker the wire, the stronger the tie.
Goal: put tightly linked nodes in one group, without saying how many groups.
The whole rule: look at your neighbours' current labels,
and join the label with the largest total weight.
Each step looks at one node and its neighbours only.
Two words first: a name is identity and never changes;
a label is membership and can be rewritten.
At the start, each node's label is its own name.
C's turn. A has already switched to label B.
Add up the weights per label.
B = 5, D = 2, E = 1: C takes label B.
It is total weight that counts, not the number of neighbours.
Asynchronous: visit A to E in turn; each change takes effect at once.
A: switches to B.
B: keeps B.
C: switches to B.
D: switches to E.
E: keeps E.
Round 1 changed three nodes.
Round 2: every node votes again.
Nothing changed, and only now is it stable: 2 rounds, cut 3.
There are three ways to stop: stable, a full round with no change;
cycle, a state that repeats;
limit, the round cap. Only stable counts as converged.
Switch to synchronous updates: everyone reads the same old snapshot.
A sees B, B sees A: they swap, then swap back.
The state repeats: that is a cycle, not convergence.
Three knobs change the outcome.
Reverse the order: 3 rounds, other label names, the same groups.
Raise C–D to 10: the groups become AB | CDE, cut 5.
Four things to keep.
Fast, local, no K;
but the result depends on the rules,
and nothing balances the groups. Try it yourself in the lab below.

chapters.title: 一 · 异步为什么会停
二 · 同步为什么振荡

transcript.text: 规则还是那一句：跟着邻居里权重最大的标签走。
这一部回答四个问题。
把 cut 当成一个计数器。开始时每条边都被切开：cut = 18。
A 改为 B：这 5 的权重不再被切开，cut 减 5。
B 不变，cut 也不变。
C 改为 B：这 5 的权重不再被切开，cut 减 5。
D 改为 E：这 5 的权重不再被切开，cut 减 5。
E 不变，cut 也不变。
A 不变，cut 也不变。
B 不变，cut 也不变。
C 不变，cut 也不变。
D 不变，cut 也不变。
E 不变，cut 也不变。
规律：异步改一次标签，cut 正好减少“新票 − 旧票”。
如果只在新标签的票严格更多时才改，
每次改动 cut 至少降 1，
而 cut 不能低于 0，
所以改动只能有限次：异步更新一定停下。
平票也改的规则不在这个论证之内。
同步就不同了：所有点同时根据旧快照改。
星形图：中心随叶子改，叶子随中心改。
于是两边互换标签，cut 一直是 4。
第 3 轮回到第 1 轮：周期为 2 的循环。
课程的 G01 同步也一样：cut 停在 17，周期 2。
二分或接近二分的结构，最容易这样来回交换。
本课程的判定：完整一轮零变化才算 stable。
每轮结束记下整张标签表，重复出现就报告 cycle。
原论文每轮随机打乱顺序，平票也随机。
所以它换了判据：每个点的标签都是邻居中最多的之一，就停。
访问顺序会改变什么？G01 的全部 120 种顺序：
分组都一样，只有轮数在 2 和 3 之间变化。
24 单元电路试 300 个随机顺序：
287 次分成 8+8+8、cut 2；13 次多切开一组，cut 21。
多数顺序找到三块；
少数顺序让中间一块被两个标签瓜分，停在一个更差的稳定状态。
代价：一轮里每个点读一遍邻居，每条边被读两次。
通讯录 61 条联系：每轮 122 次读取，3 轮就停。
相比之下，穷举分法根本数不完。
只要轮数少，总工作量就和边数成正比。
再看一个陷阱：两个三角形，中间一座桥。
平票取最小：所有点最后都成了同一个标签，cut = 0。
cut 最小的分法就是“全部一组”。这个规则没有任何力量阻止合并。
换成平票取最大，恰好分开两个三角形。
给组大小设上限 U = 3，结果不再依赖平票的运气。
常见的改法有两类。
限制组大小的版本，正是多层划分器里常用的粗化手段。
此外，随机顺序多跑几次，比较结果的波动。
回到 24 单元电路，给每组设上限 U = 4。
标签传播分出 7 个小组，每组不超过 4 个单元。
每组收缩成一个点：24 个单元的图变成 7 个点的小图。
在小图上划分，再逐层展开、细化。这就是多层划分的第一步。
四句话带走：
异步加严格改进，一定停；
同步可能永远交换；
规则要写清楚；它快，但需要约束才能用来划分芯片。
The rule is unchanged: follow the label with the most neighbour weight.
This film answers four questions.
Treat the cut as a counter. At the start every edge is cut: cut = 18.
A switches to B: 5 of weight is no longer cut, so the cut drops by 5.
B stays, and so does the cut.
C switches to B: 5 of weight is no longer cut, so the cut drops by 5.
D switches to E: 5 of weight is no longer cut, so the cut drops by 5.
E stays, and so does the cut.
A stays, and so does the cut.
B stays, and so does the cut.
C stays, and so does the cut.
D stays, and so does the cut.
E stays, and so does the cut.
The law: one asynchronous change lowers the cut by exactly new votes − old votes.
If a node changes only when the new label has strictly more votes,
each change lowers the cut by at least 1,
and the cut cannot go below 0,
so there can only be finitely many changes: asynchronous updates stop.
Rules that also change on a tie fall outside this argument.
Synchronous updates are different: every node changes at once, from an old snapshot.
A star: the hub follows the leaves while the leaves follow the hub.
So the two sides trade labels and the cut stays at 4.
Round 3 repeats round 1: a cycle of period 2.
G01 under synchronous updates does the same: the cut sits at 17, period 2.
Bipartite and near-bipartite structures swap like this most easily.
This course's test: stable means a full round with no change.
Store the labelling at each round end; a repeat is reported as a cycle.
The paper shuffles the order each round and breaks ties at random.
So it uses another test: stop when each node holds one of its neighbours' most common labels.
What does the visit order change? All 120 orders on G01:
the groups never change; only the rounds vary between 2 and 3.
On the 24-cell circuit, 300 random orders:
287 give 8+8+8 with cut 2; 13 split a group in two, cut 21.
Most orders find the three blocks;
a few let two labels share the middle block, and it stops in a worse stable state.
Cost: in one round every node reads its neighbours once, so every edge is read twice.
The 61 contact ties: 122 reads per round, stable after 3 rounds.
Exhaustive search, by contrast, cannot even be counted through.
With few rounds, the total work grows in proportion to the number of edges.
One more trap: two triangles joined by a bridge.
Ties to the smallest: every node ends up with one label, cut = 0.
The lowest cut of all is “everything in one group”. Nothing in the rule resists merging.
With ties to the largest it happens to split the two triangles.
Cap each group at U = 3, and the result no longer rests on luck with ties.
Two common fixes.
The size-constrained version is a common coarsening step in multilevel partitioners.
Besides that: run several random orders and compare how much the results move.
Back to the 24-cell circuit, with a cap of U = 4 per group.
Label propagation forms 7 small groups, none over 4 cells.
Each group contracts to one node: the 24-cell graph becomes a 7-node graph.
Partition the small graph, then expand and refine level by level: the first step of multilevel partitioning.
Four things to take away:
async with strict improvement always stops;
sync can trade labels forever;
state your rules; it is fast, but partitioning a chip needs constraints.
